points: 1 Mechanism: two stages, unsupervised left-to-right LM pre-training (L1), then supervised fine-tuning of the same model with an added linear output layer, plus an auxiliary LM objective weighted λ = 0.5; the only new parameters are W_y and delimiter embeddings (p. 3, pp. 4-5)

2 Task-specific input transformations (traversal-style) instead of task architectures: entailment = premise $ hypothesis; similarity = both orderings, representations added element-wise; QA/commonsense = [z; q; $; a_k] per answer, softmax over answers (p. 4)
3 Architecture: 12-layer decoder-only Transformer, masked self-attention, 768-d states, 12 heads, 3072-d feed-forward, GELU, learned position embeddings, BPE with 40,000 merges (p. 4)
4 Pre-training data: BooksCorpus, over 7,000 unpublished books, chosen for long contiguous text (vs the sentence-shuffled 1B Word Benchmark used by ELMo); token-level perplexity 18.4 (p. 4)

5 Recipes: pre-training with Adam, max LR 2.5e-4, 2000 warmup updates, cosine annealing, 100 epochs, batches of 64 sequences of 512 tokens, dropout 0.1; fine-tuning with LR 6.25e-5, batch 32, 3 epochs, linear decay with 0.2% warmup (pp. 4-5)
6 Withheld: no parameter count, compute or training time, and no seeds, run counts or variance are stated
7 Headline: new state of the art on 9 of 12 datasets with a single task-agnostic model, many baselines being ensembles; GLUE overall 72.8 vs 68.9 previous best (p. 1, pp. 5-7)

8 Wins with baselines: MNLI-m/mm 82.1/81.4 vs 80.6/80.1 (Stochastic Answer Network 3x); SNLI 89.9 vs 89.3; SciTail 88.3 vs 83.3 (CAFE); QNLI 88.1 vs 82.3 (GenSen); Story Cloze 86.5 vs 77.6; RACE 59.0 vs 53.3 (BiAttention MRU 9x); CoLA 45.4 vs 35.0; STS-B 82.0 vs 81.0; QQP 70.3 vs 66.1 (Tables 2-4)
9 Losses: RTE 56.0 vs 61.7 (multi-task BiLSTM + Attn); SST-2 91.3 vs 93.2 (Sparse byte mLSTM); MRPC 82.3 vs 86.0 (TF-KLD) (Tables 2 and 4)

10 Analysis and ablations: full model average 74.7; without pre-training 59.9 (the '14.8% decrease'); without auxiliary LM 75.0 (auxiliary objective helps only NLI tasks and QQP); single-layer 2048-unit LSTM 69.1 (5.6 drop, wins only on MRPC); each transferred layer helps, up to 9% on MultiNLI; zero-shot heuristics improve steadily over pre-training (pp. 7-8, Table 5, Figure 2)
